full_judgment:
2. Facts leading to the filing of the appeal are that respondent No.1 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 425 of 1984 in the court of Upazila Munsif (now the Assistant Judge), Mathbaria for declaration of her title in 10 acre land out of 5'12 acres land of Plot No. 294 as fully described in the schedule to the plaint. In the plaint, it was stated, inter alia, that 'Ka' scheduled land of R. S. Khatian No. 226 at an annual rent of taka 35, 10 annas and 3 paisa had been owned by Abdul Barek, Abdus Somed, Kulsum Bibi and Montazuddin in equal share; Kulsum Babi being the owner and in possession of 4 annas share died leaving behind only son-Yakub Ali as her heir; Kulsum Bibi during her life time did not distribute her property to any body else by any wasiyatnama either written or oral; during the last S. A. operation, 4 annas share of Momatzuddin was correctly recorded in the name of his heirs in S. A. Khatian No. 80; the remaining 12 annas share was recorded in the name of Abdul Barek, Abdul Somd and Yakub Ali, but in the S. A. Khatian, 2 annas, 13 gandas, 1 kara and 1 kranti was wrongly recorded in the name of Yakub Ali instead of 5 annas, 6 gondas, 2 karas, 2 krantis; the plaintiff was entitled to inherit 7 gondas, 2 krantis and 3 til share out of 5 annas, 6 gondas, 2 karas, 2 krantis left by Yakub Ali who died leaving behind 3 (three) sons and 7 (seven) daughters and a wife; the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land along with other co-sharers; the plaintiff being one of the daughters of late Yakub Ali filed Mutation Case No. 20M (1)/1982-83 for mutation of her name in respect of her share of the suit land and her name was mutated in her share of the suit land and her name was mutated in the case khatian. But defendant No. 1 filed another mutation case being No. 18M/82-83 denying her right, title to the suit land and hence she was compelled to file the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1, 4, 25-34 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Kulsum Bibi used to possess 4 annas share in R. S. Khatian No. 226; her husband-Nasaruddin, eldest son, Sobed ali and daughter Sonaban died during her life time and her only son Yakub Ali survived; Kulsum Bibi before her death executed a wasiyatnama on the 7th kartick, 1357 BS covering all her landed properties; by the said wasiyatnama, she granted 20 bighas land for mosque and madrasha, 10 bighas to her paternal cousin, Menazuddin for life interest and the remaining 12 (twelve) annas share to the 3 (three) sons of Yakub Ali. The property which she had inherited from Sabed Ali was given to Salimuddin to the extent of his life interest and out of the remaining property to the extent of 4 annas was given to Sabed Ali's Abdus Samad and the remaining properties of 12 annas was given to Yakub Ali's sons. After the demise of Kulsum Bibi, her son-Yakub Ali implemented the wasiyatnama and as per stipulation of the wasiyatnama, he transferred 20 bighas land in favour of mosque and madrasha by two registered waqf deeds he gave the remaining properties to his 3 (three) sons and subsequently, on 04.01.1958, the beneficiaries of Kulsum Bibi executed and registered a partition deed which was attested by Yakub Ali and as such, the plaintiff as the daughter of Yakub Ali was not entitled to get any relief in the suit and the suit was liable to be dismissed.
